info.description: A streaming AI agent backend. `/v1/messages` mirrors the Anthropic Messages API (with additive `provider` and `metadata.session_id` fields); the `/v1/sessions` endpoints manage conversations and let you list a user's chats and replay transcripts.
info.title: bepilot API

post.description:
Accepts an AG-UI `RunAgentInput` and streams the turn back as AG-UI protocol Server-Sent Events: `RUN_STARTED`, `TEXT_MESSAGE_START` / `TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT` / `TEXT_MESSAGE_END`, `TOOL_CALL_START` / `TOOL_CALL_ARGS` / `TOOL_CALL_END` / `TOOL_CALL_RESULT`, then `RUN_FINISHED` (or `RUN_ERROR`). Each frame is a `data:` line whose JSON carries a `type` field.
`threadId` maps to a bepilot session: pass an existing session id to continue a conversation, or leave it empty to start a new one (the new id is returned in `RUN_STARTED.threadId` — persist it for the next turn). Only the last user message drives the turn; history is loaded server-side. `state` and `context` are folded into the system prompt for this turn. `tools` are bound as client-executed tools: the agent may call one, but bepilot only emits the `TOOL_CALL_*` frames and ends the run — the client must execute the tool and send the result back as a `tool` message on the next run. `forwardedProps` is accepted but has no defined effect. A request whose `messages` carries no user turn is treated as a history replay for an existing `threadId` (CopilotKit issues this when a thread becomes the active one in the UI): the response is `RUN_STARTED` + `MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT` (the session's persisted messages) + `RUN_FINISHED`, with no new turn run or saved. Such a request naming an empty or unknown `threadId` is a 400, since there is nothing to replay.
A thread runs one turn at a time, but a message never has to wait for it. If a run is already in progress on the thread, the new message is handed to it — the model reads it before its next step — and this request answers immediately with an empty `RUN_STARTED` + `RUN_FINISHED`; the reply appears on the stream of the run that is in progress. A short stop message ("stop", "dừng", "hủy") interrupts the run in progress instead: it keeps what it produced and ends with a normal `RUN_FINISHED`, and the message then runs as a normal turn.

post.description:
Stores one file (PDF, JPEG, PNG or TIFF) and answers at once with `202` and the document in status `pending`; the file is read in the background, page by page. Poll `GET /v1/documents/{id}` for the progress (`pages_done` / `pages_total`) until the status is `ready` (or `failed`). Every page is read by OCR and, when a vision model is configured, by it as well; numbers the two readings disagree on are put back to the vision model, replaced only when it is sure, and otherwise noted as unverified in the page.
The same file uploaded again by the same user returns the existing document (`duplicate: true`, status `200`) without reading it again; one that had failed is queued again. With `session_id`, the document is attached to that session: every question asked on the session then gets the full text of its documents.
post.summary: Upload a document to be read in the background

parameters.description: Session to attach the document to
parameters.name: session_id

200.description: the same file was already uploaded

post.description:
The body is an Anthropic Messages request whose last user message carries the files as `document` (PDF) or `image` content blocks with a base64 `source`, and the question as `text` blocks. Every file is stored as a document (as `POST /v1/documents` does; the same file uploaded before is reused) and attached to the session (`metadata.session_id`, or a new session titled from the question). The files are read in the background.
With `stream: true` (or `Accept: text/event-stream`) the stream stays open while the files are read, sending `document_progress` events (and `ping` frames), then answers like `/v1/messages`: the agent gets the full text of every document of the session. Without streaming, the answer is `202` with the documents and the session as soon as the files are stored; ask on the session with `/v1/messages` once they are `ready` (a session whose documents are all ready already is answered at once, `200`). The documents stay attached: later questions on the session need not send them again.
post.summary: Send files and a question in one request

parameters.description: Anthropic Messages request with document / image blocks
parameters.name: request

post.description: Reads one uploaded file (PDF, JPEG, PNG or TIFF) with docpipe: a PDF is rendered page by page, every page is read by TurboOCR and, when a VLM is configured, re-read by it into markdown. Returns the markdown of every page and of the whole document. A page that could not be read carries an `error` and the rest still return; when no page can be read the response is `502`. The request, the file and the result are stored (`document_requests`, `document_files`).
post.summary: Read a PDF or image into markdown

post.description:
Runs one agent turn. With `stream: true` (or `Accept: text/event-stream`) the response is Server-Sent Events using Anthropic frame types (`message_start`, `content_block_start`, `content_block_delta`, `content_block_stop`, `message_delta`, `message_stop`, `ping`, `error`) plus the extension events `tool_execution_start` / `tool_execution_stop`. `message_start.message.session_id` is a bepilot extension carrying the session the turn was persisted under — capture it (when `metadata.session_id` was omitted, a new session is created) and pass it back as `metadata.session_id` on the next call to continue the conversation. Otherwise a single JSON message is returned, whose `session` field carries the same information.
A session runs one turn at a time, but a message never has to wait for it. If a turn is already running on the session, the new message is handed to that turn, which reads it before its next step: the response is `202` with `{"type":"steered"}` (or, when streaming, a single `steered` event) and the reply arrives on the stream of the turn that is running. A short stop message ("stop", "dừng", "hủy") instead interrupts the running turn, which keeps what it produced and ends with `stop_reason: "interrupted"`, and the message then runs as a normal turn.
Documents: `metadata.document_ids` attaches uploaded documents (`POST /v1/documents`) to the session. Every turn of a session with documents gives the agent the full text of every page of every document, in the system prompt (never in the stored history), and runs at temperature 0 unless the request sets one. While a document is still being read, a streamed request waits for it, sending `document_progress` events; a buffered one gets `409`. A failed document gives `422`; a turn that would not fit the model's context window (`documents.context_window`) gives `413`.

failed_pages.description: pages that could not be read (ready documents)

status.description: Status is pending (waiting for a worker), processing, ready or failed.

token_count.description: approximate tokens of the full text (ready documents)

unverified_numbers.description:
UnverifiedNumbers counts numbers the vision model and OCR read
differently and that were not confirmed; each is noted in its page.

error.description: set when the page could not be read

text.description:
Text is the plain OCR text of the page (only on /v1/documents/messages
records; the parse response leaves it out).

content.description: string, or an array of content blocks

history_token_budget.description:
HistoryTokenBudget (bepilot extension) caps the approximate number of
tokens of conversation history sent to the model this turn. Oldest
messages are dropped first; the latest user message is always kept, even
if it alone exceeds the budget. 0 or omitted uses the server default
(agent.history_token_budget); a negative value is rejected.

document_ids.description:
DocumentIDs (bepilot extension) attaches uploaded documents
(POST /v1/documents) to the session. Every turn of a session with
documents gets their full text; later turns need not repeat the ids.

markdown.description:
Markdown is every page's markdown, separated by "

request_id.description: RequestID is the stored document request (document_requests.id).

markdown.description:
Markdown is the page text given to the agent. Numbers the vision
model and OCR disagree on, and that were not confirmed, are listed
in a trailing <!-- unverified numbers: … --> comment.

numbers.description:
Numbers is the number check of the page: conflicts found, the vision
model's answers and what stays unverified.

duplicate.description:
Duplicate is set when the user had already uploaded the same file: the
existing document is returned and not read again.

UnverifiedNumbers counts numbers the vision model and OCR read
